source.title: 52B to 1T: Lessons Learned via Tele-FLM Series
source.authors: Xiang Li; Yiqun Yao; Xin Jiang; Xue-Zhi Fang; Chao Wang; Xin-Zhang Liu; Zihan Wang; Yu Zhao; Xin Wang; Yu-Yao Huang; Shuang-Yong Song; Yongxiang Li; Zheng Zhang; Bo Zhao; Aixin Sun; Yequan Wang; Zhong-Jiang He; Zhongyuan Wang; Xue-Long Li; Tie-Jun Huang

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites scaling laws as motivation, but does not test their loss curves, extrapolations, or compute-optimal allocations. Its own results concern progressive model growth and SFT.
record.gate_note: The authors state that each increase in model size produced a more pronounced rate of loss reduction, but give no held-out loss values or scaling-law fit. This does not measure the behavior specified by any claim version. The SFT benchmark results concern fine-tuning performance, not predictability from pretraining scale or loss.
record.test_reason: The paper cites scaling-law work only as motivation. It reports no held-out loss values, no power-law fits, no extrapolation from small runs, no compute-optimal comparison and no controlled shape comparison. Its results cover SFT data selection on a 52B model and procedures for progressive growth to 1T. The one loss statement is a qualitative remark about the growth process, not a scaling measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that function-preserving growth is viable beyond 100B and handles the jump from 102B to 1T, with knowledge recovered after each stage and faster loss reduction at larger sizes. They note they could not compare the 1T model with one trained from scratch or benchmark it comprehensively. They also conclude that a small SFT set (30k samples) suffices for most tasks but not for maths and reasoning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies progressive model growth, not the scaling-law measurement or fitting procedures in the cited original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: In progressive function-preserving growth from 52B to 102B to 1T, the authors report qualitatively that each size increase gave a faster rate of loss reduction. No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-reduction rate after function-preserving growth increases with the grown model's size. This is unquantified and confounded with stage hyperparameters.

record.problems: No numerical loss results or scaling-law fits are provided. The authors state that they could not compare the 1T model with one trained from scratch and could not conduct a comprehensive benchmark evaluation of the 1T model.

untested.parts: No held-out loss measurements or power-law fits in N, D or C.
No prediction from small runs checked against large runs. The text says growth was 'guided by empirical results from smaller models' but reports none.
No fixed-parameter comparison of depth and width. 'Preserve a proper aspect ratio' is stated for growth convergence, without data.
No other modality or regime with a scaling fit.
SFT benchmark scores are for one 52B model only, with no scale relationship.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: This is a technical report and preprint. The aspect-ratio remark ('critical to preserve a proper aspect ratio') could be read as touching V4, but it concerns convergence of grown models and gives no evidence, so it is not a test.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss measurements or power-law fits over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No predictions from smaller runs compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law scaling in another modality or of its persistence across training regimes.
SFT benchmark scores are reported, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents, fitting choices, or deviations from a single power law.

rows.subject: Tele-FLM series
rows.operation_detail: Progressively grew the model through the 52B, 102B, and 1T stages; authors report the loss-reduction rate increased with each size increase.
rows.measure: Rate of loss reduction during progressive growth
rows.value: Authors report a more pronounced rate of loss reduction with each increase in model size; numerical losses are not stated.
rows.note: Aggregate statement about the staged model series. It does not specify held-out loss or establish a power-law relationship, so it is not linked to a claim version.
rows.check: This is a qualitative remark with no numbers: 'each increase in model size resulted in a more pronounced rate of loss reduction'. It is measured within a single grown model across growth stages, which confounds size with stage, learning-rate schedule and tokens (2003B, 300B, 15.7B). It is not held-out loss against N, D or C, so state 'observed' cannot be checked against any version. Unlinking it is correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
